newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 21.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* A new federal tax proposal aimed at closing a loophole corporations use to sell assets tax-free could jeopardise AirTouch's plans to acquire U S West Media's domestic wireless operations for $2.3 billion in stock plus $2.2 billion in assumed debt. It also could derail America Online talks to buy CompuServe.
* Roger Ferguson Jr, a partner at consulting firm McKinsey & Co is expected to nominated for one of two open seats on the U.S. Federal Reserve Board, White House officials said.

* U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky expressed disappointment with slow pace of Japanese deregulation while releasing a report on Japan's attempts to make its auto market * Tobacco settlement talks started again, partly due to a North Carolina lawyer who played a role in bringing industry CEOs to the table.
* Market makers are starting to worry about the possibility that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission will expand new trading rules to more Nasdaq stocks because of volatility in small stocks.
* Citicorp is shifting leadership of its consumer-bank unit to train possible successors to chairman John Reed and streamline management of worldwide operations.
* Around 12,500 United Steelworkers members employed by Goodyear Tire went on strike after negotiatiors failed to reach agreement on a new contract.
* An American Association of Retired Persons plan to offer managed-care coverage to members who are retirees is being changed due to concerns it could violate federal statutes.
* British Telecommunications and MCI Communications signed an agreement with Telefonica de Espana which gives it a strong position in North America, Latin America and Europe.
* Jayhawk Acceptance said it filed a reorganization plan with a bankruptcy court under which it would repay $65 million to its primary lender Fleet Financial
* Fidelty Investment's Bart Grenier, assistant head of the equity department, is thinking of leaving.
* Cordiant is set to announce a restructuring which could involve the sale of its advertising agencies Saatchi & Saatchi and Bates Worldwide.
* Heard on the Street: Who needs cigarette ad? Billboard companies say they can manage without them. Owners of car-racing tracks such as Penske Motorsports say the same.

* Credit markets: Don't bet the house on the mortgage market. The mortgage-backed bond market has turned heads in recent weeks but few analysts suggest it will do better than hold its own in coming months.
